core_obligations: Reduce to $Y = \Spec(A)$ and $S = \Spec(R)$, and set up the Cech complex $K^\bullet$ of a finite affine open covering, together with the natural map $\Omega^\bullet_{A/R} \to K^\bullet$, its multiplication and the filtration inherited from the Hodge filtration (proof lines 2044-2092).

Choose cocycles $x_i \in K^{n_i}$ representing the classes $\xi_i$ and form the morphism of complexes $\tilde x : M^\bullet = \bigoplus_i \Omega^\bullet_{A/R}[-n_i] \to K^\bullet$ sending a form in the $i$-th summand to $x_i \wedge \omega$; the assertion becomes the statement that $\tilde x$ is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 2095-2105).

Endow $M^\bullet$ with the filtration $F^kM^\bullet = \bigoplus_i (\sigma_{\geq k}\Omega^\bullet_{A/R})[-n_i]$, making $\tilde x$ a morphism of filtered complexes, and compute $\operatorname{gr}^0M^\bullet = \bigoplus_i A[-n_i]$ together with the identification $\Omega^k_{A/R}[-k] \otimes_A \operatorname{gr}^0M^\bullet \to \operatorname{gr}^kM^\bullet$ (proof lines 2106-2116).

Use the relative generation lemma to see that $\operatorname{gr}^0\tilde x$ is an isomorphism in $D(A)$, and K-flatness of $\operatorname{gr}^0K^\bullet$ to conclude that every $\operatorname{gr}^k\tilde x$ is an isomorphism in $D(A)$ by derived tensoring with the free module $\Omega^k_{A/R}[-k]$ (proof lines 2117-2142).

Conclude by induction on $k$ from the short exact sequences of the filtrations that $\tilde x : M^\bullet/F^kM^\bullet \to K^\bullet/F^kK^\bullet$ is an isomorphism in $D(R)$ for every $k$, hence that $\tilde x$ is a quasi-isomorphism because the filtrations are finite in each degree (proof lines 2143-2154).
proof_roadmap: The Cech complex and its filtered structure (proof lines 2044-2092).
The map $\tilde x$ built from cocycles representing the classes (proof lines 2095-2105).
The filtration on $M^\bullet$ and its graded pieces (proof lines 2106-2116).
Comparison of graded pieces via the relative lemma and K-flatness (proof lines 2117-2142).
Induction on the filtration and the conclusion (proof lines 2143-2154).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that classes in the de Rham cohomology of the total space whose restrictions to each fibre form a basis make the de Rham cohomology of the total space a free module over that of the base (statement lines 2023-2041). The proof replaces the cohomology of the total space by a Cech complex with a Hodge filtration, constructs the comparison map from a sum of shifted copies of the base complex using cocycles for the given classes, and proves it is a quasi-isomorphism by comparing graded pieces: the case $k = 0$ is the relative generation lemma and the higher cases follow by derived tensoring, using K-flatness, with an induction on the filtration to finish. The filtered comparison argument is the substance, so the claim is H2 (the author states a list of standard facts about the Cech complex without proof, referring to the discussion before the spectral sequence lemma).
